requirements.title: IEEE_OVERFLOW occurrence is fixed for supported real operations and processor dependent otherwise
requirements.source: S17.3 p1.overflow-supported, p1.overflow-latitude; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF480-482.
requirements.definition: IEEE_OVERFLOW occurs for real addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, REAL conversion, and complex operation or CMPLX conversion part calculations as specified by 60559 for operands whose IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE is true; unsupported operands and real exponentiation are processor dependent.

pending.overflow-signals-for-supported-real-conv: Guard probe: two profiled real kinds convert a finite source value larger than HUGE(target), the target has IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE true, and IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_OVERFLOW,target) true. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_OVERFLOW,X). TRUE branch: execute REAL(source,KIND=target_kind) and assert IEEE_OVERFLOW signaling. FALSE branch: skip profile gap.
pending.overflow-signals-for-complex-part-calcul: Guard probe: default real kind X and double kind Y both have IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE true, IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_OVERFLOW,X) is true, and HUGE(Y)>HUGE(X). Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_OVERFLOW,X). TRUE branch operation case: multiply CMPLX(HUGE(X),0.0_X)*CMPLX(2.0_X,0.0_X) and assert IEEE_OVERFLOW signaling from the real part. TRUE branch CMPLX-conversion case: reapply the preamble, evaluate CMPLX(HUGE(0.0D0),0.0D0,KIND(0.0)), and assert IEEE_OVERFLOW signaling from conversion of the real part. FALSE branch: skip the missing support or range branch.
pending.overflow-unsupported-or-exponentiation-l: No portable oracle fixes overflow signaling for unsupported operands or real exponentiation; FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE is referenced but not applied because this latitude row records either flag state without failure.

requirements.title: IEEE_UNDERFLOW and IEEE_INEXACT occurrence definitions use processor limits and exactness
requirements.source: S17.3 p1.underflow, p1.inexact; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF480-482.
requirements.definition: IEEE_UNDERFLOW occurs for real or complex operation or assignment results whose relevant part has absolute value below a processor-dependent limit, and IEEE_INEXACT occurs for inexact real or complex operation or assignment results.

pending.underflow-limit-is-processor-dependent: No portable oracle fixes the numeric underflow threshold beyond using TINY-derived guarded operations; fixtures must not require a processor-specific boundary value.
pending.inexact-signals-for-inexact-complex-part: Guard probe: real kind X has IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(X) and IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_INEXACT,X) true. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_INEXACT,X). TRUE branch: compute CMPLX(1.0_X,0.0_X)/CMPLX(3.0_X,0.0_X), then assert IEEE_INEXACT signaling. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.underflow-signals-for-real-assignment-un: Guard probe: default real kind X and double kind Y both have IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE true, IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,X) is true, TINY(0.0D0)<TINY(0.0), and the assignment conversion of TINY(0.0D0) to default real is inexact because the stored result differs from the double source. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,X). TRUE branch: execute real_default = TINY(0.0D0) and assert IEEE_UNDERFLOW signaling for assignment. FALSE branch: skip the range, support, or exact-underflow caveat branch.
pending.inexact-signals-for-real-assignment-unde: Guard probe: default real kind X and double kind Y both have IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE true, RADIX(0.0)==2, RADIX(0.0D0)==2, DIGITS(0.0D0)>DIGITS(0.0), and IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_INEXACT,X) true. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_INEXACT,X). TRUE branch: execute real_default = 0.1D0 and assert IEEE_INEXACT signaling for assignment conversion to default real. FALSE branch: skip non-binary, support, or precision branch.

requirements.title: Exception flags are quiet or signaling, initially quiet, set by exceptions, and mutable by status procedures

FALSE branch: skip unsupported optional flag except p10 quiet branch.
pending.exception-occurrence-sets-associated-fla: Guard probe: use S17.3-001 through S17.3-004 supported-operation branches. TRUE branch: those rows apply the FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE for their associated FLAG, execute the operation, and IEEE_GET_FLAG(FLAG) returns .true. FALSE branch: skip unsupported flag.

pending.entry-signaling-flag-restored-on-return: Guard probe: IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_OVERFLOW,X) true. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_OVERFLOW,X). Caller sets IEEE_OVERFLOW signaling and calls the helper used for entry-quiet observation. TRUE branch: after helper returns without setting the flag, caller observes IEEE_OVERFLOW .true. again. FALSE branch: skip.

requirements.source: S17.3 p10; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF480-482.
requirements.definition: The processor is not required to support IEEE_INVALID, IEEE_UNDERFLOW, or IEEE_INEXACT; an unsupported exception flag is always quiet.

accounting.rationale: Exception occurrence rules mix required supported cases and processor latitude.
Required overflow occurrence for supported operations and complex part calculations.
Overflow for unsupported operands and exponentiation is processor dependent.
Required divide-by-zero occurrence for supported division and complex part calculations.
Divide-by-zero for unsupported division and negative-exponent exponentiation is processor dependent.
Invalid operation and assignment occurrence rule.
Underflow occurrence rule with processor-dependent limit.
Inexact occurrence rule.
Flag state, initial value, exception setting, setters, and persistence are split.
Flags have quiet/signaling state determined by IEEE_GET_FLAG.
Initial flag value is quiet.
Associated exception sets flag, subject to exact-underflow caveat.
IEEE_SET_FLAG and IEEE_SET_STATUS can change status.
Signaling flag remains signaling within a procedure until set quiet.
Procedure entry/return flag quieting and restoration rules.
Specification-expression evaluation may signal.
Intrinsic-procedure preservation, final-result latitude, and intermediate-calculation rule are split.
Normal intrinsic procedure execution preserves entry flag values.
Final overlarge or invalid-NaN results may signal.
Intermediate calculations not affecting result do not change flags.
Relational table rule and conversion latitude are split.
Real-result numeric relations signal invalid according to Table 17.1.
Operand conversions may signal instead of or in addition to comparison invalid.
NOTE explains 60559 predicate behavior and is not normative.
Normative table mapping Fortran relational operators to 60559 predicates.
Complex equality/inequality invalid signaling and conversions are permissive latitude.
Dead operation exception flag result is processor dependent.
No-extra-operation prohibition and permitted OR latitude are split.
Exceptions shall not signal solely from operations beyond those required or permitted.
Permitted evaluation may signal divide-by-zero.
Unsupported invalid, underflow, and inexact flags are always quiet.
